forced_star.reason: Degree balance gives sixteen vertices in each color. The three center neighborhoods are disjoint fifteen vertices of the other color by their geodesic distances. Its unique remaining vertex z therefore centers every edge of G[J], a five-edge star, and the three centers have no incident star edge. L and R are disjoint because a vertex in both gives an endpoint path of length four. Star leaves cannot occupy both sides and a B port cannot meet both sides, since either would give an endpoint path of length six.

side_bounds_and_middle_data.reason: Each endpoint-neighborhood row has four side neighbors. A side of size four closes a proper K5,5 component, hence both side sizes are at least five. Counting the noncenters gives nL+nR=13-r and r=t+u<=3. A middle nonleaf meets all B; a middle star leaf meets all but one B. Thus each port has side arity s_i=4-r+m_i in [1,4], sum m_i=u.

port_parts_and_u_positive.reason: The right part is nonempty by connectedness. Left degree balance is sum s_i=5nL-25+u, positive when u>0. If u=0 and the left part were empty, p0,A,L,z would be a proper component. For u=0 all arities equal s=4-t in [1,4]; the right balance s|BR|=5(nR-4) and coprimality force 5 to divide |BR|, contradicting 1<=|BR|<=4. The right incidence mass is at least five and each port has arity at most four, giving |BR|>=2 and |BL|<=3.

hand_derivation: Let b=|BL| and k=sum_BL m_i. Solve (4-r)b+k=5(nL-5)+u with 1<=b<=3, 0<=k<=u, nL+nR=13-r and nL,nR>=5.
For (r,u)=(1,1), the only solution is (nL,nR,b,k)=(6,6,2,0), giving one partition row.
For (r,u)=(2,1), the only solution is (6,5,3,0), giving one row.
For (r,u)=(2,2), solutions are (5,6,1,0) and (6,5,3,1). The right total two in the first has partitions 2 and 1+1, and the second is unique, giving three rows.

For r=3, both sides have size five and b+k=u. At u=1,2,3 this gives respectively one, three and five partition rows. The last case has (b,k)=(1,2),(2,1),(3,0) with respectively one, two and two partitions.

The resulting multiplicities are 1+1+3+1+3+5=14. Every TeX row agrees with the symbolic JSON table. Each middle leaf has exactly one missing port, so the multiplicities contain all middle incidence data up to the specified role permutations.

incidence_necessity_and_all_row_realizab.reason: For any distinct side subsets of prescribed port arity and any S of size 5-u, hL<=|BL|+1<=4 and hR<=|BR|<=4. Side balances give total omission degree five on a side of size five and ten on a side of size six. Singletons with prescribed multiplicities realize the first. In the second, every degree is at most four, strictly below half the total ten, so consecutive stub blocks paired at opposite positions give a loopless five-edge multigraph. Its parallel edges index distinct endpoint-row vertices. Thus every table row is feasible and every permitted choice is a simple five-regular graph of order thirty-two.

connectedness_and_girth.reason: The nonempty X0 joins all ports; every other core vertex has four port neighbors, and z joins u>0 core vertices. Both port parts are nonempty, each port has a side neighbor, and every side vertex meets an endpoint row. The endpoint centers connect all their row vertices, giving a single component. Bipartiteness excludes triangles. Twenty other-U incidences through the five neighbors of one U vertex cannot be distinct among fifteen other U vertices, so a four-cycle exists.

diameter_upper_bound.reason: Core vertices pairwise share a port and are at distance two. Each endpoint, and every false twin of it, is at distance exactly four from every core vertex. For nonisolated core vertices the left endpoint uses a star leaf; the right endpoint uses one of at least two right ports, avoiding the one missing port. Every A row meets S because |L minus S|<=3-t<4. Every C row meets a right-port-supported side vertex: otherwise the required right incidence total 5(nR-4) would be squeezed into nR-4 omitted vertices of capacity at most four. Hence every V vertex is within three of some core. Every remaining U vertex is within two of a core unless it is an endpoint false twin. Combining these estimates with core pair distance two gives every pair distance at most eight, including the endpoint-twin exception.

diameter_lower_bound_and_marked_geodesic.reason: Deleting the core separates the two endpoints. Each endpoint has distance four to every core vertex, so the endpoint distance is at least eight. Left and right length-four paths through p4 have disjoint roles away from p4 and concatenate to a length-eight geodesic. Thus the diameter is exactly eight and p4 can be its marked midpoint.

ordinary_isomorphism.reason: Equality of full open neighborhoods is intrinsic. Its classes are independent, their mutual adjacency is complete or empty, and a weight-preserving quotient isomorphism lifts to an ordinary graph isomorphism. The use of the full uncolored quotient correctly handles twins beyond the visibly repeated core/row classes and avoids unjustified additions or factorial division across root, orientation and skeleton choices.

general_k_section.reason: For order6k+2 the color sizes are3k+1 and the unique extra vertex centers K1,k. Side size at least k and nL+nR=3k-2-t-u imply q=1+t+u<=k-1. Degree balances give exactly (6). If u=0, s=k-1-t lies in[1,k-1], and gcd(k,s)=1 excludes u=0 by forcing k to divide |BR|. Prime k therefore excludes u=0. The k4,t1,u0 example satisfies the necessary arithmetic and is correctly not asserted to be realized or to satisfy a general converse.
